prompt: Process-lifecycle registry and reaper: track and close every process a flow pipeline spawns. Pipelines leak processes (chrome-devtools-mcp servers + Chrome, vitest/node/npm/dev-server toolchain processes that reparent to PPID 1 when their session dies). Point-of-use teardown plus PR #491's ancestry-based flow-browser-teardown has two structural blind spots: ancestry cannot see reparented processes, and identity-by-name is dangerous for generic argv0s. Build a flow-spawn launch wrapper + per-slug registry at ~/.flow/state/procs/<slug>.jsonl (own process group per launch; kill(-pgid) survives reparenting; startEpoch closes pid reuse), a per-class kill-policy reaper (default TERM->wait->KILL on pgid; mcp-server SIGTERM to pid only, never escalated), failure-surfacing terminal-state wiring replacing the silent '|| true' sites, a crash-path orphan sweep over dead-session registry rows, and resolution of the flow done --orphans / flow-browser-teardown --orphans flag collision. Extend the merged PR #491 code, never duplicate it; the AGENTS.md point-of-use standing rule may be revised.

features.title: flow-spawn launch wrapper + per-slug process registry
features.description: Build the process-lifecycle registry seam: a new `bin/lib/proc-registry.ts` owning the row schema {pgid, pid, startEpoch, slug, class, argv} and append/read/compact operations over append-only JSONL at ~/.flow/state/procs/<slug>.jsonl, plus a `bin/flow-spawn.ts` launch wrapper that starts the given command in its OWN fresh process group (Bun.spawn detached:true — verified on this host that child pgid == child pid), captures startEpoch via bin/lib/liveness.ts pidStartEpoch, records the row, and passes through stdio/exit code. Include a list/report mode (`flow-spawn --list <slug>` or equivalent) and full unit tests plus one live sleeper-tree test asserting pgid isolation and row shape. Purely additive: no kill paths, no pipeline wiring changes in this feature. Bun runtime, import.meta.main gate, chmod +x, tests next door. Part of epic `process-lifecycle-registry-reaper-track` (feature `proc-registry-spawn`) — design at `.flow/epics/process-lifecycle-registry-reaper-track/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides D1 (the identity channel and row schema) behind a stable lib API — the walking-skeleton root every other feature consumes.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN a command is launched via flow-spawn THE SYSTEM SHALL start it in its own fresh process group (ps -o pgid= shows pgid == pid) and append a parseable JSONL row {pgid, pid, startEpoch, slug, class, argv} to ~/.flow/state/procs/<slug>.jsonl
WHEN the wrapped command exits THE SYSTEM SHALL propagate its exit code unchanged
WHEN the registry file or procs directory is absent THE SYSTEM SHALL create it on first append

features.title: Registry-driven reaper with per-class kill policies
features.description: Extend the teardown surface (bin/flow-browser-teardown.ts and/or a shared bin/lib module — extend, NEVER a parallel duplicate helper) with a registry-driven reap engine: for each row in ~/.flow/state/procs/<slug>.jsonl, verify liveness AND startEpoch match (bin/lib/liveness.ts pidStartEpoch; a mismatch means pid reuse — skip, never signal), then dispatch by class: default class = SIGTERM -> bounded wait -> SIGKILL on kill(-pgid); mcp-server class = SIGTERM to the server pid only, never the group, never escalated (only the server's shutdown() closes Chrome cleanly). The existing ancestry walk (resolveSessionPid/selectMcpServers with the argv-position-anchored isMcpServerCommand predicate) demotes to a FALLBACK for registry-miss cases, unchanged in mechanism. Ship --dry-run and --json first-class; typed JSON result including per-row outcome (reaped/skipped-epoch-mismatch/already-dead/failed). This is destructive-action kill-path code: strictest review lens, dry-run-first live verification, never signal a sibling session's processes; any contrived validation pipeline runs in ~/code/me/pokemon with --no-auto-merge and must not merge. Part of epic `process-lifecycle-registry-reaper-track` (feature `reaper-kill-policies`) — design at `.flow/epics/process-lifecycle-registry-reaper-track/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides D2+D3 (kill-policy encoding and the registry-first/ancestry-fallback layering) behind one reap CLI with a typed JSON result.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN a registered default-class row is live with matching startEpoch THE SYSTEM SHALL SIGTERM its process group, wait a bounded interval, and SIGKILL the group only if still alive
WHEN a registered mcp-server-class row is live THE SYSTEM SHALL send SIGTERM to that pid only — never the group, never a harsher signal
WHEN a row's pid is dead or its startEpoch mismatches THE SYSTEM SHALL skip it with a per-row outcome and send no signal
WHEN the registry has no row covering an in-session chrome-devtools-mcp server THE SYSTEM SHALL fall back to the existing ancestry-scoped teardown path

features.title: Route pipeline spawn sites through flow-spawn
features.description: Adopt the flow-spawn wrapper (or the proc-registry lib directly) at the spawn sites flow itself owns, assigning a class per site: ui-smoke/ui-validation dev-server launches (skills/pipeline/flow-pipeline/references/ui-smoke-pass.md and flow-ui-validate), backgrounded flow-ci-wait invocations, and test-runner/script launches made by flow helpers (e.g. flow-pre-commit's child processes) — NOT harness-owned spawns (the chrome-devtools-mcp server is launched by Claude Code and cannot be wrapped; it stays on the ancestry path). Update the relevant skill prose/runbook blocks and helper code together so real pipelines produce registry rows. Keep inline-env port discipline intact (never write config files). Include tests asserting each adopted helper records a row with the intended class. Part of epic `process-lifecycle-registry-reaper-track` (feature `spawn-site-adoption`) — design at `.flow/epics/process-lifecycle-registry-reaper-track/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides D1's adoption surface — which launch sites flow owns and how each maps to a class — producer-side only, no kill-path changes.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN a ui-smoke dev server is launched by the pipeline THE SYSTEM SHALL record a registry row with a dev-server-appropriate class
WHEN flow-ci-wait is launched in the background THE SYSTEM SHALL record a registry row for it
WHEN a spawn site is harness-owned (chrome-devtools-mcp server) THE SYSTEM SHALL leave it unwrapped and documented as ancestry-fallback territory

features.title: Failure-surfacing terminal-state reap wiring + standing-rule revision
features.description: Replace the 8 terminal-state `flow-browser-teardown --json || true` call sites in skills/pipeline/flow-pipeline/SKILL.md with the registry-driven reap invocation in a shape that never blocks the terminal transition but NEVER silently no-ops: when the reap fails to run or exits unclean (helper missing from PATH, non-zero exit, malformed JSON), the failure is surfaced in the gate/terminal summary output the user reads and recorded durably (state.json or a .flow-tmp artifact). Add a bin/skill-md-lint.test.ts check forbidding a bare `|| true` regression at these sites. In the same PR, apply the user-authorized standing-rule revision: rewrite AGENTS.md 'Don't leave spawned resources running' and SKILL.md's 'Resource cleanup' section into the three-layer contract (point-of-use first, registry reap as guaranteed backstop, orphan sweep as crash-path net) so docs and behavior change together. Reap correctness over an empty registry (ancestry fallback) means this does not depend on spawn-site adoption. Part of epic `process-lifecycle-registry-reaper-track` (feature `terminal-state-wiring`) — design at `.flow/epics/process-lifecycle-registry-reaper-track/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides D4 (the never-block-but-never-silent invocation shape) and D6 (the revised rule text) behind the terminal-state runbook contract.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN the reap helper is missing from PATH or exits non-zero at a terminal state THE SYSTEM SHALL surface a visible failure marker in the terminal-state output and record the failure durably
WHEN the reap fails THE SYSTEM SHALL still complete the terminal state transition (never blocks)
WHEN skill-md-lint runs THE SYSTEM SHALL fail on any terminal-state reap site regressed to a bare '|| true'
WHEN AGENTS.md and SKILL.md are read after merge THE SYSTEM SHALL describe the layered cleanup contract instead of the point-of-use-only rule

features.title: Crash-path registry orphan sweep + --orphans flag convergence
features.description: Add the crash-path sweep: select registry rows whose RECORDING SESSION is dead (session pid + startEpoch liveness via bin/lib/session-identity.ts and bin/lib/liveness.ts), report them, and reap them through the per-class kill engine only with explicit --yes (report-only default); never touch a row whose recording session is alive (never signal a sibling session's processes). Keep the existing shape-heuristic sweeps (selectOrphanBrowsers/selectOrphanMcpServers) for unregistered strays. Resolve the --orphans flag-name collision: `flow done --orphans` sweeps state FILES while `flow-browser-teardown --orphans` sweeps PROCESSES — converge process sweeps under one documented surface (recommended: a `flow reap` verb with flow-browser-teardown --orphans delegating/deprecating; flow done --orphans unchanged), and update help.ts/docs accordingly. Destructive-action code: dry-run-first live verification; contrived validation pipelines run in ~/code/me/pokemon with --no-auto-merge and must not merge. Part of epic `process-lifecycle-registry-reaper-track` (feature `orphan-sweep-convergence`) — design at `.flow/epics/process-lifecycle-registry-reaper-track/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides D5 (the dead-session sweep criterion and the converged command naming) behind one documented sweep surface.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN a registry row's recording session is dead THE SYSTEM SHALL report the row, and signal it only under --yes using its class kill policy
WHEN a registry row's recording session is alive THE SYSTEM SHALL never signal it
WHEN a user consults help/docs THE SYSTEM SHALL present state-file sweeping and process sweeping under distinct, non-colliding names
